IMPORTANT - importMap data quality issue found and NOT applied: comparing the supplied $IMPORT_MAP against the assembled graph's 'imports' edges initially looked like 13 missing cross-batch edges (app/pricing.py -> app/excel.py, app/pricing.py -> app/ingest.py, and 11 test-file -> app/config.py/app/db.py/app/pricing.py edges). I added these 13 edges, then verified each against the actual source files with grep before finalizing. Every single one of the 13 failed verification: app/pricing.py has no import of app/excel.py or app/ingest.py anywhere (only unrelated docstring/comment occurrences of the word 'ingest'); tests/test_ai.py, tests/test_config.py, tests/test_labor_policy.py, tests/test_pricing.py, tests/test_pricing_lifecycle_hardening.py, tests/test_pricing_llm.py, tests/test_source_lifecycle_api.py, and tests/test_security.py do not import app/config.py directly (test_config.py only references 'app.config' inside a Python source string passed to a subprocess in one test, not as a real import); tests/test_export.py only imports 'from app import export' (not app/db.py or app/pricing.py). I reverted all 13 edges, restoring the graph to the merge script's original output (482 nodes, 883 edges, 95 imports edges) verified clean (0 dangling, 0 duplicate edges).

Recommend flagging upstream: the $IMPORT_MAP appears to have a systematic false-positive pattern attributing 'app/config.py' as an import target to many unrelated test files (at least 8 confirmed instances), plus at least 3 other spurious entries (pricing.py->excel.py, pricing.py->ingest.py, test_export.py->db.py/pricing.py). This looks like either stale/cached scan data or a scanner that matches on substrings/fixture usage rather than actual import statements -- worth investigating the project-scanner's import-map extraction logic before trusting it for future runs.

Separately, importMap's 'tests/test_reports.py -> app/reports.py' entry was also not actionable: app/reports.py does not exist anywhere in the repo. Reading tests/test_reports.py shows it actually imports 'from app import db' and 'from benchmarks.reports import (...)' -- both already correctly represented in the graph. This is a second, independent example of importMap inaccuracy (likely from the duplicate-key JSON construction artifact called out in the dispatch context), reinforcing the recommendation above.
